title: Tenant resource fencing controller for per-tenant GPU isolation and QoS
creator: Marcus Liu
description: Implement a cluster-side controller (Tenant Resource Fencing Controller, TRFC) that enforces per-tenant GPU isolation and QoS policies across the Dedicated fleet. Goal is to provide predictable throughput guarantees for reserved tenants while limiting noisy neighbor impact from bursty tenants. TRFC will coordinate with autoscaler, scheduler, and runtime to apply soft and hard fences: token-bucket style burst credits, lane assignment, proactive cgroup placement, and eviction/graceful pause policies when quotas are exceeded.
acceptance_criteria: Controller can apply per-tenant fence policies from the TenantReservation API within 5s of reservation change
Reserved tenants maintain 95th percentile throughput within 10% of target under 2x noisy background load in the same pool
Burst credit accounting prevents a tenant from consuming >120% of committed tokens over a sustained 60s window without triggering soft-eviction flow
Soft-eviction triggers graceful pause + cache flush with application-level hinting; hard eviction forcibly reclaims lanes and records a detailed audit event
Operator can override fencing for emergency maintenance via the Console and see audit entries in the activity log
implementation_steps: Design API extension: TenantReservation.spec.fenceProfile (bandwidthRPS, burstTokens, laneAffinity, preemptionPolicy)
Build TRFC controller as a standalone service that watches reservation CRDs and fleet metrics, publishes lane assignments to scheduler and runtime
Integrate token-bucket library with persisted counters in Redis for cross-node accounting
Implement soft-eviction flow: notify runtime to enter draining mode, persist KV-cache snapshots, mark requests with 'throttled' response header
Implement hard-eviction: scheduler forcibly migrates or pauses pods and reclaims GPU allocations; emit audit log and incident metric
Add autoscaler hooks: when tenant approaches sustained utilization above threshold, trigger reserved-scaling or circuit-breaker fallbacks
Expose Console controls: per-tenant throttle window, burst token tuning UI, and real-time lane utilization charts
Add e2e tests and chaos experiments to validate fairness under variable load
testing_plan: Unit tests for token-bucket accounting and race conditions
Simulated cluster tests with 100 tenants of mixed reservation sizes to measure throughput and tail latency
Back-to-back noisy neighbor experiments: inject synthetic spike traffic and verify reserved tenant SLOs hold
Fault-injection: controller restart and Redis failover while preserving counters and correctness
Integration tests with autoscaler to confirm scale-ups/downs respect tenant fences
rollout_plan: Alpha: deploy TRFC to staging fleet with feature flag enabled for 5 pilot tenants (internal teams)
Canary: enable for 20% of production tenants in a single region; monitor lane utilization and error rates for 72h
Gradual ramp: 20% -> 50% -> 100% over 2 weeks with detailed post-mortems at each step
Operator training: runbook for manual overrides and incident mitigation
Fallback: instant disable flag that removes fences and reverts to existing soft-throttling behavior
notes: This ticket focuses on cluster-level enforcement; a follow-up will add SDK-level flow control to surface backpressure to customers
We intentionally separate soft-eviction (graceful) from hard-eviction (forceful) to minimize user-visible errors while preserving throughput guarantees
Prefix-based cache isolation (tenant-keyed KV cache) will be coordinated with TRFC but implemented in runtime team workstream
Kernel affinity tagging (for MIG-like partitioning on supported HW) is listed as a stretch goal depending on testing window
